latest_apis.rationale: Consistently on the current stable generation of Qwik/Qwik City — version pinned to the release from five days ago, all primitives (routeLoader$, useSignal, useNavigate, node middleware, vite plugins) match what the 1.20.3 starter generates; nothing legacy and no framework-internal hacks.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:34 — global fetch (Node 24 native), no axios/node-fetch polyfill
app/src/lib/api.ts:49 — new URL(url).pathname for API path parsing
app/src/lib/urls.ts:12 — URLSearchParams for query construction, omitting defaults
app/src/routes/index.tsx:91-96 — native <input type=search>/<select> with labels, no client-side filter framework
app/src/global.css:4-48,104-107 — CSS custom properties for every token plus logical properties (margin-inline/padding-inline) and grid auto-fill
app/src/global.css:78-83 — :focus-visible instead of JS focus handling
platform.rationale: Reaches for the platform first throughout: native fetch, URL/URLSearchParams, native form controls, modern CSS with custom properties and logical properties, zero polyfills or hand-rolled replacements. Only gap is no abort/timeout on outbound fetch, which is robustness rather than platform avoidance.

evidence: app/package.json:12-14 — runtime deps are exactly qwik + qwik-city at latest stable (1.20.3); nothing else shipped

app/package.json:20 — vite ^5.4.0, locked to 5.4.21 (app/package-lock.json:3658) — an EOL major (vite.dev/releases supports only 8.x/7.3/6.4 as of Oct 2026); the current Qwik starter ships vite: latest and Qwik 2.0 requires Vite >= 6
app/package.json:18 — typescript ^5.6 resolves to 5.9.3 (app/package-lock.json:3486), current
app/package.json:17 — @types/node ^24 matching the Node 24 runtime

dependencies.rationale: Minimal, mostly modern set with runtime deps at the latest stable. One questionable pick: Vite is pinned to an EOL major two releases behind, which forfeits security patches and adds a mandatory toolchain migration before the Qwik 2 upgrade.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:32 — apiFetch returns Promise<any>; app/src/lib/data.ts:8,15,27,28 — records kept as any
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:40,53,141,143 — every PokeAPI field accessed via any casts, so API shape changes are invisible to tsc
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:299 — '?game=' URL built by inline template string (and unencoded), while home filters go through lib/urls.ts:17 homeUrl()

app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:318, app/src/routes/moves/[name]/index.tsx:105, app/src/routes/abilities/[name]/index.tsx:58, app/src/routes/types/[name]/index.tsx:106 — head title ternary duplicated across four routes
app/src/entry.node-server.ts:10 — manifest passed to createQwikCity even though entry.ssr.tsx:4-7 already injects it; the 1.20.3 starter does not pass it here
app/src/entry.node-server.ts:7-14 — no ORIGIN/getOrigin/trustForwardedHeaders; 1.20.3 middleware docs say request-derived origin is 'not recommended for production' behind a proxy
app/src/lib/api.ts:8-21 — single in-process promise cache and concurrency limiter: all upstream API access localized to one module
churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, URL building and configuration are well localized and the adapter/server boilerplate tracks the generated starter, so a framework patch upgrade touches almost nothing. But the API boundary is untyped end to end (Promise<any) and URL/head-title logic is duplicated across routes, so a change in API shape or title convention ripples through every route file.

findings.issue: Vite pinned to ^5.4 (installed 5.4.21) — an EOL major: vite.dev/releases lists only 8.x/7.3/6.4 as supported in Oct 2026, the current Qwik starter ships vite: latest, and Qwik 2.0 (in rc) raises the minimum to Vite >= 6, so this pin guarantees an extra migration step and no security patches in the meantime.
findings.suggestion: Bump to vite ^7 (still within qwik's peer range >=5 <8) or at minimum ^6, and let the lockfile track a supported major.

findings.issue: apiFetch returns Promise<any> and every consumer casts raw PokeAPI payloads as any (data.ts:8,15; pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:40,53), so a change in API shape — exactly what the live-data-overlay tests simulate — produces no compile-time signal.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal response interfaces (NamedAPIResource, PokemonRecord, SpeciesRecord, TypeRecord...) at the api.ts boundary and have apiFetch be generic over them; keep the derived view models in data.ts.

findings.issue: Outbound fetches have no AbortSignal/timeout, so a hung upstream API stalls SSR requests indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Pass AbortSignal.timeout(...) (with a generous limit) to fetch and drop rejected promises from the cache as already done.

findings.issue: createQwikCity is configured without ORIGIN/getOrigin/trustForwardedHeaders; the 1.20.3 node middleware docs state that deriving the origin from the incoming request is not recommended for production, and the spec assumes a reverse proxy in front of the server.
findings.suggestion: Read ORIGIN from the environment (defaulting to API_BASE_URL origin or PORT) or provide getOrigin, and document the PROTOCOL_HEADER/HOST_HEADER option in a comment.

findings.issue: manifest is passed into createQwikCity although entry.ssr.tsx:4-7 already supplies it via @qwik-client-manifest; the official 1.20.3 starter does not pass it here, so this is drifted hand-maintained boilerplate.
findings.suggestion: Drop manifest from the createQwikCity options and keep it only in entry.ssr, matching the generated starter verbatim.

findings.issue: The ?game= query is assembled with an inline template string (and no encodeURIComponent) while the home filters all go through lib/urls.ts homeUrl() — URL-building logic is split across two places.
findings.suggestion: Add a pokemonUrl(name, game) helper (or a general query-helper) in lib/urls.ts so query serialization stays in one module.

findings.issue: The 'title or Not found – Pokédex' head ternary is duplicated across four routes (moves:105, abilities:58, types/[name]:106, pokemon/[name]:318).
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared headTitle(d: {enName} | null) helper so the document-title convention changes in one place.

summary: The app is squarely on Qwik's current stable release (1.20.3, five days old at review time), uses its current-generation primitives throughout, and mirrors the official node-server starter so closely that a patch upgrade is a near no-op. Its main forward-looking weaknesses are the untyped any-based API boundary that hides upstream shape changes from the compiler, and a Vite 5 pin that is EOL and below Qwik 2.0's coming Vite >= 6 floor. Net: ages well, with two well-defined fixes before it ages worse.
